label: Procedure and flow
use_when: The subject is a process that runs in stages over time, such as a request lifecycle, a startup sequence, a commit protocol, or a compilation pipeline, and the reader wants to follow what happens at each stage.
topic: The process and the span the article follows, phrased the way a developer would search for it (e.g., 'What happens between calling save() and the row reaching disk'). Not a symptom and not a how-to.
thesis: One declarative sentence claiming what the order or the division of the stages guarantees or makes possible: a claim a competent engineer would want justified. A list of the stages is not a thesis.
focus_points: Three or more items, one per stage, in the order the stages run. Each item names the stage and what it is responsible for.
outline_rules: no_invented_problem: Do not invent a failure, incident, or problem scenario to motivate the subject. The article explains the process itself.
stage_boundaries: Each step region covers one stage. Consecutive step regions must connect: what one stage hands on is what the next one receives.
one_running_example: Choose one concrete input (a single request, one transaction, one source file) and follow it through every step region's example.
review_rules: weak_relevance: Remove a step region if the process reads the same without it, i.e., what the previous stage hands on is exactly what the next stage receives.
write_rules: no_invented_problem: Do not open with or build toward a failure story. Motivate the article by what the reader will be able to trace after reading it.
one_running_example: Follow the same concrete input through every stage instead of starting a new example in each section.
handoffs: Begin each step section from what the previous stage handed on, so the reader never loses the thread between stages.

regions.outline: key_sentence defines the process in one sentence: what goes in and what comes out. elaboration names the stages in order and the point of view the article takes (core_message).
regions.write: Open with two or three sentences that define the process and state the article's point of view (core_message). Then name the stages in order, introduce the running input, and end with the question the rest of the article answers.

regions.outline: One stage of the process. heading names the stage. key_sentence states what this stage is responsible for. elaboration states what it receives, what it does, and what it hands on. example shows the running input at this stage.
regions.write: Say what the stage receives, what it does to it, and what it hands on, showing the running input with code, a log excerpt, or a text diagram. Explain why this work happens at this point in the order where the order matters.

regions.outline: The whole flow. key_sentence restates core_message in light of the stages. elaboration says what the order of the stages guarantees from end to end.
regions.write: Trace the running input once more from the first stage to the last in a few sentences, and restate core_message in that light. Close with a short list of questions the reader should now be able to answer. Add no new claim. The heading names what the order of the stages guarantees, not 'Conclusion' alone.
